quest.title: Vimana Agama: Jazari's Chapter
quest.description: You were finally able to get inside the Ruin Golem. If it can be activated, gaining access to the underground ruins should be a simple matter...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's so much bigger in here than Paimon thought!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Of course it is! Wait, this is a moment for that famous phrase, is it not?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: "Behold. Thousands of years of ancient Khaenri'ah history lie before us!"

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Oops, got carried away there. This is a famous quote by Iskandar, a Vahu{RUBY#[S]Aetiology}mana sage. Wait. Haven't you read his biography?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I've read about it countless times in books, but this is the first time I've seen it in person, and that's why I can't contain my excitement.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look at all these vines. It must have been a really long time since anyone last came here.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: According to the text named "The Review of Research on Issues Related to the Ruin Golem in Ancient Khaenri'ah," the last scholar who managed to get inside a Ruin Golem for systematic research was Pir Kavikavus.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I'm sure you don't know this, but Pir Kavikavus was one of the greatest scholars in Kshahrewar's history. Kavikavus earned the rank of Herbad before hitting thirty — a genuine academic genius.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: With his achievements, he would have become a sage sooner or later. But he met with an accident during an expedition, and his research results were lost.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Ever since then, Kshahrewar has gone downhill. If he had lived longer, perhaps I wouldn't be worrying about expenses day and night like this.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: By the way, it's my academic ambition to follow in Pir Kavikavus' footsteps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, forget your academic ambition for now. Our next step is to...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh, then we need to activate this big guy first.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Right. By activating the Ruin Golem, I can get valuable experimental data, which will then serve as the basis for a breakthrough in my research.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: One has to make some waves to outdo one's predecessors, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So let's get this thing working, then! There's got to be some mechanism here... You know, the kind of thing that lights up when pressed?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Hmm... I do recall there being one. According to our records, once the Separation Valve in the steering cabin is turned on, the Ruin Golem will be activated.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: But as I told you before, all ruin machines are driven by the dark power of their cores. And the cores of the Ruin Golem have been sealed underground.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Even if we got into the steering cabin, the conventional method will not work.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: In fact, we can't even start this lift right before us, so how will we get to the steering cabin at the top?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, you're right... So what do we do now?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Wait! I do have the most authoritative research permit granted by the Akademiya, but that doesn't mean we can damage this machine as we please.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: As the saying goes, "when one door closes, another opens." And in any case, I'm positive that the people of Khaenri'ah surely took this scenario into consideration.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The Akademiya's research shows that the early ruin machines also had a backup power system, perhaps because the techniques that allowed them to utilize this dark power were still in their infancy.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Unlike the cores that supply almost unlimited energy, this power system comprises a series of small power relays.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The power sources of these devices are energy blocks that store pure energy extracted from the Ley Lines.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: According to Vahu{RUBY#[S]Aetiology}mana researchers, this power system most likely had been in widespread use long before the first ruin machine was ever built in ancient Khaenri'ah.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: As I stated earlier, the Ruin Golem is an early model, so it must have one of those backup power systems.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: The core power cabin is at the bottom. Let's get down there first.

choices.text: Just tell me what to do next.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, the core power cabin is at the bottom. Let's get down there first.

choices.text: You're implying that there's an unconventional route.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm, did you forget that we're here to investigate the underground ruins? Academic research is important, sure, but we need to figure out how to get this big guy started first.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Well, knowledge is boundless. I do not intend to have my learning shackled.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! It's starting up!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: What do you think? The machinery in the Ruin Golem, whether it's a relay or a trap door, can be powered by this Energy Block.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But nothing seems to have changed at all...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, because this backup system comprises a series of small power relays.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: In other words, we have to work all our way up from the bottom, and the system can only function when all the relays have been connected.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: All of them...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Given the damage to the Ruin Golem, it will be quite difficult for it to run at full power.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: But just as you were activating this relay, I found this in the power room.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: It seems to be the blueprint for the Ruin Golem. Perhaps its maintenance crew left it here.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: According to this blueprint, we only need to connect several key relays to start this machine...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: At the very least, we'll be able to start this lift and go up to the steering cabin.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds questionable...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, there's nothing else we can do, so we might as well try activating the lift first, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, aren't you coming with us?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I'll stay here and take pic— no, study the internal structure of the Ruin Golem. That's also important work.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Besides, I'm a scholar. There's little I could do to assist you directly in your task. But if you have any technical problems, I'll be here for you.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Look at the ingenious machinery all around. What a masterpiece of human civilization!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: This is valuable information for research. I've gotta record all it down.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Back so soon? Well, I'm still studying the load-bearing structure of these components here. But it's impressive that you got the lift started!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You were just guessing about the activation thing, weren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well... Come on, I've only read about it in books.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Just so you know, there are no more than three people in the entire Akademiya who can read this blueprint. So guessing it right does mean something!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Anyway, now that the lift is working, we should be able to access the steering room above by activating the relays on the middle level.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I see... The mid-level gear should be in the power room. We need to activate all four relay units.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: If we can't find an Energy Block that works, it is also possible to temporarily remove them from the device. It's fine as long as they're all connected in the end.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I'll keep waiting for you here then.

talks.objective: Connect all four relays in the middle

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Huh? What were you guys doing up there? I thought I heard a truly incredible racket while I was studying this inductive circuit.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, whatever you're doing, please keep it down. If there's any trouble with the machine here, it'll be hard for me to explain it away in my report to the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Pilot? Are you joking?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Even people of Khaenri'ah couldn't live for hundreds of years.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Anyway, I assume you've got the relays in the middle connected, yes?

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: I'm almost done here as well. Come. Let's go up to the steering cabin at the top.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Just like before, we simply need to connect the power system to the steering cabin to activate the Ruin Golem's control systems.

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Umm, are you and this child both... Alright, okay. You know what? I'll write two recommendation letters to the Akademiya. This way, the two of you can get along in future as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that's not what's happening here at all!

talks.objective: Connect to the pilot cabin power system

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Besides this dark stone slate, nothing else here seems to be of value.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Stone slate? Don't underestimate it. If we can get the control system running, then we can see the outside world through it.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: The control system here looks like it can still work. Ancient Khaenri'ah's creations really are amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I never thought I would have this chance in this lifetime. But now it seems that once I complete this research report, winning the Pir Kavikavus Prize is only a matter of time now...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then let's try and start this machine. Paimon can't wait!

response.speaker: Jazari
response.text: Now, now, we shouldn't rush anything. We need to follow the instructions!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Let me see. According to these specifications, I should first press... Huh, which one is it...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: And what did I say about following the instructions...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We didn't really get it to do anything...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Its arm just, y'know, fell off! Paimon's pretty sure the machine itself is to blame!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Fine, I'll record it as an experimental accident, then. Ugh... I do hope that this won't diminish my report in any way.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Anyway, it seems like we won't be able to start the Ruin Golem again, so there's no point in me keeping you here.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I know you're here to investigate the contamination of the underground ruins, but I'm afraid that the Ruin Golem won't be of much use to you now.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Even so, you may see some unexpected progress as a result of what you did.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Well, I shall not keep you any longer. I have my research to get done here, in any case.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: You can come and look for me once your work is done... if I haven't been disciplined for destroying the Ruin Golem yet.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Once that happens, I can help you apply for the research project on the Chaos Cores.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I'll be the one in charge of the project, of course. But don't worry, I'll give you half the funds.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Anyone can embark on an academic career as long as they have the desire to learn, so go for it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks just like the big robot Paimon once visited!

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Oh? You have been inside another Ruin Golem?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! In the desert, someone named Afratu asked us to look into machines just like this one.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Afratu? Darn it, don't tell me he has also got his eyes on the title of "Well-known Ruin Golem Researcher."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, I don't think that's the case...

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: I remember that guy to be a Vahumana Researcher, and this shouldn't interest him.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: That's not totally impossible, though.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: After all, that's where Iskandar, the sage saying "Behold. The thousand-year history of ancient Khaenri'ah lies before us!", comes from.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Enough about the "well-known researcher" thing. Compared to the one we saw, this seems really deserted.

dialogues.speaker: Jazari
dialogues.text: Of course.
